module.bimi.checks: Reads the BIMI record, checks the SVG logo (HTTPS, size, Tiny PS profile, active content) and the VMC/CMC brand certificate (validity, usage, domain), and verifies DMARC is enforced.
module.bimi.fix:
Check DMARC first: it must be enforced at 100% (`p=quarantine` or `p=reject`, with no `pct=` below 100), otherwise no mailbox provider shows the logo (see the Email security module).
Prepare the logo as SVG Tiny PS: a square image, `version="1.2"` and `baseProfile="tiny-ps"` on the `svg` element, a square `viewBox`, no script, no bitmap image and no external link, preferably 32 KiB or less. Conversion tools are listed in the BIMI Group guide.
Publish the logo on a site with valid HTTPS (HTTP 200 response, content type `image/svg+xml`).
Get a brand certificate from a Mark Verifying Authority: a VMC for a logo registered as a trademark, a CMC otherwise. It must cover the sending domain. Publish the PEM file you receive on the same site, over HTTPS.
Publish a single TXT record `default._bimi.example.com` that holds the logo URL (`l=`) and the certificate URL (`a=`); see the snippet for an example.
Expired or soon-to-expire certificate: renew the VMC or CMC with the authority and replace the PEM file before the deadline. Once it has expired, the logo is no longer displayed.
Logo or certificate reported as non-compliant: fix the point the finding names (content type, profile, square shape, non-HTTPS URL, domain not covered, BIMI usage missing from the certificate), then publish the file again.
If you do not want to use BIMI, delete the `default._bimi` record rather than leaving it incomplete.
Check with `dig +short TXT default._bimi.example.com` and `curl -I` on both URLs (HTTP 200), then run the scan again; the logo can take a few days to appear in inboxes.
module.bimi.fix_snippet:
# DNS
default._bimi.example.com.  IN  TXT  "v=BIMI1; l=https://example.com/bimi/logo.svg; a=https://example.com/bimi/certificate.pem"
# dig
dig +short TXT default._bimi.example.com
# curl
curl -sI https://example.com/bimi/logo.svg
curl -sI https://example.com/bimi/certificate.pem
module.bimi.title: BIMI
module.bimi.why: BIMI shows the brand logo in recipients' inboxes: it builds trust and helps people recognise genuine messages, but requires an enforced DMARC.
